name: Kola Valvill Ramar Temple, Thiruvelliyangudi
deity: Vishnu as Kola Valvilli Raman, reclining, with the festival lord Sringara Sundaran and the Goddess Maragathavalli — the shrine of Venus (Shukra)
period: A Divya Desam of the Chola country on the Pazhavaru, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thiruvelliyangudi near Kumbakonam, Vishnu reclines as Kola Valvilli Raman, Rama of the beautiful bow — a Divya Desam sung by Thirumangai Alvar, honoured as the Vaishnava shrine of Venus.

sections.history: Thiruvelliyangudi is one of the 108 Divya Desams and one of the shrines of Chola Nadu, a village on the north bank of the Pazhavaru, some 19 km from Kumbakonam. Thirumangai Alvar sang its lord in ten verses of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Its name is drawn from Velli, the Tamil name for the planet Venus, Shukra, and the shrine is counted among the Vaishnava Navagraha temples of the Tamil country as the abode of Venus; it was also known of old as Bhargava Kshetra, after Shukra's lineage. The temple is maintained today under the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of Tamil Nadu.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner, the temple enshrines the lord reclining on the serpent, facing east, beneath the Pushkalavartaka Vimanam; the festival image is Sringara Sundaran, and the Goddess Maragathavalli has her own shrine. Four sacred waters are named for Shukra, Brahma, Indra and Parasara, the Parasara tank being the temple's own. Local tradition points out a Garuda with four hands, holding the discus and conch.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that when Mahabali poured water to grant Vamana his three steps, Shukra, his preceptor, blocked the spout as an insect, and lost an eye when the lord cleared it with a blade of grass; he worshipped here, and tradition holds that his sight was restored. It tells too of Mayan, the architect of the asuras, who longed to see Rama without conch and discus — so the lord gave them to Garuda and appeared as Kola Valvilli Raman.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Vaishnava festivals of the year — Vaikunta Ekadashi, the days of Rama and the days of Thirumangai Alvar — with processions through the village. As the shrine of Venus it also draws pilgrims making the round of the planetary temples of the delta.
sections.experience: A quiet village shrine in the paddy country beyond Kumbakonam, Thiruvelliyangudi rewards the pilgrim who comes for its rare form of Rama, reclining yet bearing the bow. Visit it as part of the Divya Desams of the delta or the round of planetary shrines, and look for the four-handed Garuda.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi is busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thiruvelliyangudi lies about 19 km from Kumbakonam, reachable by road through the delta villages; Kumbakonam has the nearest railway station of size, and Tiruchirappalli the nearest airport.
